title: International Salary-to-Rent Ratio Index 2026
subtitle: Benchmarking housing affordability by measuring central 1-bedroom rent as a percentage of individual net take-home pay.
metaDescription: The 2026 Salary-to-Rent Index evaluates median net professional income against HUD, ONS, and DSC rental data across 10 major global cities.
citationString: LivWorthy Research Institute. (2026). International Salary-to-Rent Ratio Index 2026. https://www.livworthy.com/reports/salary-to-rent-index
methodologyNotes: Housing costs reflect median 1-bedroom apartment rents in central business districts.
Income baselines reflect median professional worker earnings from municipal and national labor agencies.
Rent burden threshold: Below 30% is considered financially sound; 30–40% is moderate; above 40% represents significant housing cost distress.

primarySources.name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD FMR FY2026)

summaryInsights: Zurich and Berlin offer the most favorable salary-to-rent profiles (<29% of net pay), affording median professionals substantial uncommitted savings.
New York City and London exhibit the most severe housing burdens, where central 1-bed rents absorb 45% and 48% of median net professional take-home pay respectively.
Austin provides substantially lower rent burdens (31%) than coastal US technology hubs like New York (45%) and San Francisco (41%).
